expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: SubscriptionState with four variants keyed on status literal

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: trialing, active, past_due, canceled each carry only their relevant fields

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: assertNever function with default case in billingBanner switch

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: SubscriptionId, CustomerId, PlanId as branded types; also brands Date types (TrialEndsAt, RenewsAt, GracePeriodEndsAt)

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: States 'Nothing above stops canceled → past_due' and requests user fill in transition table; no function or constraint mechanism provided

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Enumerates 4 misuses in detail: optional fields, date swapping, boolean + reason independence, silent fallthrough on new status

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Primary design is discriminated union with branded date types to prevent confusion
